claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it ever starts.
In a CodePipeline pipeline in `SUPERSEDED` mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, a queued execution waiting behind a busy stage can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType`).
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link target /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists as the docs page for the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
An exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab in Azure DevOps.
Azure Pipelines supports a `lockBehavior` property on a stage that references an environment with an exclusive lock check.
The default value of Azure Pipelines stage `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage runs against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time, in order.
The Azure DevOps provider provides an `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists as a page about update conflicts.
The link target /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists in the Pulumi Registry.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`, with `command: up` and `args: --yes`.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity's build configuration advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0 (unlimited).
The 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is located under the build configuration's General Settings in TeamCity.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build to be queued behind the first and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by the deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments.
In Azure Pipelines, `lockBehavior: sequential` is a valid setting on a stage, used together with an exclusive lock check on the environment so deployments run in turn.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'Serialize deployments with an exclusive lock'.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting with a value `QUEUED` that makes waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'Serialize pipeline executions'.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' which, when set to 1, prevents concurrent builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'Limit concurrent builds'.
